titel: Peter Pan, by J. M. Barrie. Part VII.

faehigkeiten.grund: Dynamik weder belegt noch ausgeschlossen: keine Merkmale gefunden, aber eine unveraenderte Wiederholungsprobe beweist nichts

einzeiler: The children return to the nursery, Wendy grows up, and Peter continues his visits.
kurzfassung: The children return home to their remorseful parents, who have been living in Nana's kennel to mourn them. Years pass, and Wendy grows up, marries, and has a daughter of her own named Jane. Eventually, Peter returns for Jane, passing on the tradition of the spring cleaning visits.
stichpunkte: Mr. and Mrs. Darling mourn the missing children, with Mr. Darling living in Nana's kennel out of remorse.
Wendy, John, and Michael finally return to the nursery and are joyfully reunited with their parents.
The lost boys also return from the island and are eventually adopted by the Darlings, later growing up to lead ordinary lives.
Wendy slowly grows up, loses the power to fly, marries, and has a daughter named Jane.
Peter Pan visits an adult Wendy once more, realizing she has grown up and can no longer fly with him.
Jane begins flying with Peter for his spring cleaning visits, continuing the generational cycle.

clips.hook: Mr. Darling moves into the kennel
clips.text: Overcome with guilt and remorse after the children run away, Mr. Darling decides to live inside Nana's old kennel.
Upon arriving back at the nursery with Tinker Bell, Peter immediately decides to close and bar the window to prevent Wendy from returning to her mother.

clips.hook: Peter refuses to become a man
clips.text: Frightened by the prospect of growing a beard and attending school, Peter firmly rejects Mrs. Darling's offer of adoption.

clips.hook: The adult lives of the lost boys
clips.text: The former lost boys grow up to have conventional adult jobs, with Michael as an engine-driver, Slightly a lord, and Tootles a judge.
When Wendy tells Peter she can no longer fly because she has grown up, he panics and begs her not to turn on the light.

beschreibung:
Peter Pan, the boy who wouldn't grow up, steals Wendy and her brothers away to a magical world called the Neverland. They come face to face with a fairy named Tinker Bell, the Lost Boys, savages, pirates, mermaids, a crocodile that ticks, and Peter's nemesis -- Captain Hook!
The book is filled with excitement and wonder, and teaches that with happy thoughts, and a little help of pixy dust, you can fly! Peter Pan inspires children everywhere to believe!
